newsitem.title: JAPAN: WEEK AHEAD - Tokyo stocks likely to search for floor.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD - Tokyo stocks likely to search for floor.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to keep up their search for a floor in the coming week, brokers said, with the benchmark Nikkei 225 moving in a range of 20,000 to 21,000, carrying the risk of momentary dips below.
"Despite the Nikkei's fall below the 20,500 level this (past) week there doesn't seem to be a feeling that the market has hit the bottom," Yasuo Ueki, general manager at Nikko Securities said.
"Foreign investor selling which had been forcing domestic investors onto the sidelines lately is abating but they are not quite ready to buy yet."

On Friday, the key Nikkei 225 ended 166.20 points, or 0.81 percent, higher at 20,633,06, unable to recoup the losses of over 870 points accumulated in the week before. It closed at 20,739.97 on Friday.
Brokers said the expected formation this week of a new Japanese government and the U.S. presidential elections on Tuesday were likely to keep most investors glued to the sidelines.

They said the market was concerned about a possible shift in the current long-standing strong-dollar policy if President Bill Clinton is re-elected, which, in the long run, could hinder Tokyo share prices.

Masaaki Higashida, strategist at Nomura Securities, said that low interest rates were giving the market support, but unwinding of arbitrage-linked positions were sending cash stocks down with it and the situation was likely to last.
"Rather than major issues, investors will opt to trade in speculative issues until trade direction is clearer," a middle-sized brokerage broker said.
